title: My secret fear: Is it me?
cue: Their confidence made me less confident.
script: Everyone seemed to know the perfect way to use AI. Better prompts. Better tools. Better systems. The more confident the advice got, the less confident I felt.
source: Proposed first-person wording based on Dave's account of his motivation, supplied in this conversation. Typographic opening; no staged portrait or claim about a photographed event.
delivery: Address the room, not the slide. Give the final sentence space. AI adds an extra spoken syllable, not a pause.

title: Is it me? / What works?
cue: I changed the question: what actually works?
script: Buy the course. Comment ‘AI agents.’ Get the perfect system. I was comparing myself to everybody else’s claims. So I changed the question: what actually works?

delivery: Treat the first three clauses as familiar examples, not impressions of a specific vendor. Small pause before the new question.

title: Dave Sifry / 2,416 reviews
cue: Introduce myself, then the experiment.
script: BTW, I’m Dave Sifry. I founded Technorati and co-founded Linuxcare. I got pissed with all those vibes. So I ran the tests. two thousand four hundred sixteen AI code reviews, across fifty pull requests and five mature open source codebases.
source:
Biographical facts supplied by Dave in the organizer’s accepted speaker description: founder of Technorati and co-founder of Linuxcare.
REPORT.md, campaign overview and §2.2. 2,416 healthy runs across the campaign, not 2,416 independent pull requests. The planned matrix has 72 configurations; 66 have complete coverage of the six primary PRs. Primary analysis selects one run per configuration per PR; it does not measure repeat-run variance. The original benchmark and executed hidden-defect validation supply distinct parts of the answer key.
delivery: Briefly introduce yourself after the two opening emotional beats. Then move directly to the study. The small generated waving portrait is based on Dave’s supplied photograph. Do not add a career list or extra statistics.

title: The comparison manifold
cue: Model, method, reasoning.
script: Which model? One prompt or a harness? How much reasoning? Could China’s open-weight GLM models compete? I tested eight models, three review methods, and low, medium and high reasoning.
source: REPORT.md §2.2. Eight tested models: Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5, Sonnet 5; GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Terra, GPT-6 Astra; GLM-5.3 and GLM-5.3-Flash. Three methods: an engineered single prompt, Compound Engineering, and metareview. Three effort levels: low, medium, high. The planned 72-cell matrix has 66 complete cells on the primary six-PR sample; six Fable harness cells have partial coverage. The open-weight comparison covers these two GLM deployments, not every Chinese or emerging model. GLM-5.3 used a hosted 4-bit quantized build; the Flash serving build was not documented. Geographic background for GLM: Z.ai/Zhipu official company page, https://www.zhipuai.cn/en/about .
delivery: Give each question a beat. The family names support the question, not a roster to read aloud. Do not say all 72 configurations were complete.

title: 42 known bugs
cue: The detailed comparison used six pull requests and forty-two known bugs.
script: For the detailed comparison: I whittled it down to the six most knotty pull requests, Forty-two bugs humans had found. That gave me part of the answer. But the answer key was incomplete.
source: REPORT.md §§2.2 and 3.1. Six severity-selected PRs. Forty-two original benchmark goldens.
delivery: Preserve the six-PR scope. The answer key was incomplete; that is not a measured comparison of human reviewer performance.

The universe is campaign-discovered and not exhaustive. title: Evidence you can rerun
cue: The isolated reproduction fails before the fix and passes after.
script: Here’s one verified defect: re-importing a deleted post crashed. An isolated test reproduced it. Add the missing guard, and the test passes. Evidence you can check.
delivery: Name the defect in ordinary language. Indicate the failing result, then the passing result. Do not read code or a stack trace. This is evaluator verification, not an automatic repair demo.
source: Verified defect 4-D14. Original isolated reproduction log: RESULT: FAIL: NoMethodError: undefined method `raw' for nil:NilClass. Fixed log: RESULT: PASS. The minimal patch adds return if post.nil? after post = embed.post in the real app/models/topic_embed.rb. The isolated Ruby test stubs surrounding dependencies, so this is not a full Rails integration run or proof of a new PR regression. The audit explicitly retained it. Primary artifacts at https://github.com/dsifry/harnesseval/tree/8f634b68664751527a9ad0123d1a082dd70a0931/analysis/verified_gold/4/B08-topicembed-re-import-crashes-when-the-embedded-post-was-/defects/4-D14 . See also analysis/verified_gold/WITHDRAWALS_AND_DEDUP_2026-09-18.md, line 47. The benchmarked harness did not perform this evaluator verification automatically.

title: Inside a review harness
cue: A harness coordinates the review jobs and combines the findings.
script: A harness runs checks, assigns focused reviews in parallel, then combines findings. Same model, different jobs. I maintain metareview, one of the harnesses tested.
source: Illustrative architecture based on REPORT.md §2.2 and the pinned metareview_realistic.py adapter. Security, Architecture and Testing-quality are examples of actual reviewer lenses, not the full roster. The adapter runs its deterministic command and context scaffold before dispatching reviewers, then combines per-lens outputs. The report says eight lenses and synthesis; the pinned CLI prompt says nine and explicitly concatenates the findings. This diagram deliberately does not assert an exact lens count or a separate judgment step. No automatic fixing is depicted. The evaluator and its ground-truth adjudication are separate from the review harness.
delivery: Use the three active verbs to walk left to right once. Do not read every lens label. The maintainer disclosure is essential and this is the only spoken product mention.

title: The harness found more
cue: The harness found more bugs in thirty-nine of forty-two matched comparisons.
script: In matched comparisons, the harness found more verified bugs thirty-nine times out of forty-two. Same model. Same reasoning setting. The review process mattered.
source: REPORT.md matched true-gold recall comparison. Seven models, three efforts, two harness versus vanilla pairs. Observed direction, not 39 individually statistically significant effects.
delivery: Say ‘comparisons’ before introducing the count; forty-two earlier meant bugs. Leave a beat after the result. Display a noun with the number, not only 39/42.

title: 10× the tokens
cue: Harnesses used about ten times the tokens, at the median.
script: Those extra passes used about ten times the tokens, at the median. More review has a price. Did that work also need an expensive model at high reasoning?
source: REPORT.md median token multiple 10.1 across 42 matched comparisons. Token consumption is distinct from dollar cost.
delivery: Let the excessive paper trail set up the cost question. Say "at the median" aloud; keep the slide itself spare. The photograph is a generated visual metaphor, not a measured bill.

title: More thinking?
cue: I tested the reasoning settings instead of assuming high was better.
script: The reasoning dial is tempting. Turn it up, get a better review. But that’s an assumption. I tested low, medium and high to see what the extra thinking bought.
source: REPORT.md effort sweep. Only low, medium, high were tested. Generated rotary-control illustration is a metaphor, not a real product control.
delivery: Let the photograph be understood before speaking. A small turning gesture is enough; no acting routine.

title: Often, no clear difference
cue: Most comparisons were inconclusive. That does not prove equivalence.
script: Of twenty-two high-versus-medium comparisons, seventeen were inconclusive on the original benchmark score. Four favored high; one favored medium. Inconclusive doesn’t mean equal.
source: REPORT.md effort comparison on the 42-golden benchmark F1, not the 147-bug composite score. 17 unresolved, 4 favor high, 1 favor medium. Unresolved does not establish equivalence.
delivery: This is the densest concept. Point to the large inconclusive group, then briefly the other two. End on the uncertainty, not a claim that high cannot help.

title: Before you commit
cue: Review before you commit, then review the fix.
script: Review before you commit. Reproduce the failure. Fix it. Run the test. Then review the fix, too. Check the findings yourself. Find bugs before your users do.
source: Recommended developer workflow, not a measured autonomous fixing loop. The developer uses the harness for review, reproduces and verifies findings, fixes and tests the code, then re-reviews the changed code. FURTHER-RESEARCH.md treats iterative development-loop outcomes as further work. Local development describes the workflow, not local model inference. Finding bugs before users is a goal, not a production outcome measured by this study.
delivery: Follow the loop once, then return to the audience. Finding bugs before users is the goal, not a measured production outcome.

title: Use a harness
cue: Use a harness, with focused review jobs.
script: Use a harness. Give the model focused review jobs and a repeatable process. In this study, that usually found more verified bugs than asking the same model once.
source: Recommendation supported by 39/42 positive matched recall differences. It does not establish that every harness implementation helps every task.
delivery: Keep this as the first clear takeaway. Avoid saying the harness challenges its own conclusions unless the illustrated process actually includes that separate stage.

title: Use /low effort
cue: Start low, try open weights, then measure on your code.
script: Start with low reasoning. Try open-weight models. Compare what they catch, what they miss, the cost and the wait. Then choose based on evidence from your code.
source: Recommendation from the selected GLM Flash metareview low configuration. 71 bugs is total across six PRs; cost and latency are per-review means. Other configurations can have higher recall. Open weights does not imply local inference.
delivery: Distinct imperatives. This is a starting recommendation, not a universal ranking or a claim that low beat high in the high-versus-medium comparison.
